expenses.title: Deductible Expenses
expenses.deduction-split-note: This expense deducts a different rate for each tax, because they are two different questions. The supplies of a home partly used for the activity are deductible for income tax at 30% of the affected share (art. 30.2.5.ª b LIRPF) and deduct no input VAT at all, because art. 95 LIVA requires exclusive use. That is why the row can carry an income tax rate above zero next to a deductible VAT of 0.00 €.

form.vat-deduction-hint: Left blank, the input VAT is deducted at the same rate as income tax. The utility bills of a partly affected home, for instance, deduct 30% of the affected share for income tax and 0% for VAT.
form.deduction-split-hint: The same expense can be deductible at one rate for income tax and a different one for VAT, because the two follow independent rules. The utility bills of a home partly used for the activity are deductible for income tax at 30% of the affected share (art. 30.2.5.ª b LIRPF), while for VAT nothing is deductible at all: art. 95 LIVA requires exclusive use. That is why there are two boxes and not one.

category-defaults.vat-deduction-hint: Left blank, expenses in this category deduct input VAT at the same rate as income tax. Set it to 0 for the utility bills of a partly affected home: 30% of the affected share for income tax, nothing for VAT.
category-defaults.deduction-split-hint: Set it to 0 when the category gives no right to deduct VAT even though it is a deductible business cost for income tax: that is the case of the utility bills of a partly affected home, deductible at 30% of the affected share for income tax (art. 30.2.5.ª b LIRPF) and not deductible for VAT for lack of exclusive use (art. 95 LIVA).

fixed-assets.title: Fixed assets and depreciation
fixed-assets.subtitle: An asset is not deducted in the year it is bought: its cost is spread over its useful life (art. 30.2 RIRPF)
fixed-assets.dotacion-note: The yearly charge is not a movement of money: nothing leaves the bank account. It only goes into the Modelo 100 box as a deductible expense for the year.

verification.invalid: There are {count} discrepancies between the instalments and the resolution's totals. Check them against the letter before continuing.

checks.principal-total: The instalment principals do not add up to the resolution's total principal.
checks.surcharge-total: The instalment surcharges do not add up to the resolution's total surcharge.

checks.interest-accrual: This instalment's interest does not match the days it accrues over: base × rate × days / 365 (art. 53 RGR).

parts.title: Why each instalment is split in three
parts.description: You pay a single charge, but for tax purposes it is three items with different treatment. That is why each instalment creates one movement per item instead of a single one for the total.

principal.label: Principal
principal.description: It is the VAT or income tax you already owed. Paying a tax is not an expense, so none of it is deductible.

recargo.label: Enforcement surcharge

outcome.no-surcharge-note: Instalments without a surcharge create no surcharge movement: it only appears if the letter prints one.
outcome.pending-note: They are created as pending, on the due date the letter states.
outcome.models-note: Each movement enters the models the day you mark it as paid: until then it counts in neither Modelo 130 nor Modelo 100.
outcome.interest-note: Interest is created at 100% deduction and box 0203; principal and surcharge at 0%.

cross-quarter.title: Accrual and collection
cross-quarter.description: An invoice is declared in the quarter it was issued, whichever quarter the money moved in. The models for this quarter are already computed that way.

case.collected-in-another-period: Collected in Q{collectionQuarter}, but declared in this quarter: VAT and IRPF accrue on issue, not on collection.
case.collected-in-another-year: Collected in Q{collectionQuarter} {collectionYear}, already a different tax year: it is declared in this quarter and goes into the {invoiceYear} annual return, not the {collectionYear} one.
case.issued-not-collected: Issued this quarter with no collection on record: VAT accrues on issue, so it is declared now even though the money has not arrived yet.
case.declared-in-earlier-period: The money arrived this quarter, but the invoice was declared in Q{invoiceQuarter} {invoiceYear}: this quarter's models do not count it.
case.paid-without-linked-movement: This invoice is collected. What is missing is the link to the bank movement, which is common on older invoices. Without that link there is no record of the date the money arrived, so the app cannot say which quarter it was collected in. The figures do not change —it is declared in the quarter it was issued— but while the link is missing there is also no way to check whether the money arrived in a quarter later than the one that declared it. Link the movement and the date comes back.

cross-quarter.link-missing-hint: What is missing is the link to the bank movement, not the collection itself.
cross-quarter.data-integrity-note: This is not a tax warning: no figure in the models changes because of it. It is a datum the app is missing, not something you owe.
cross-quarter.data-integrity-fix: To fix it: open the invoice and link it to the bank movement the money arrived in.
cross-quarter.pay-warning: The collection date falls in a different quarter from the issue date: the invoice will still be declared in Q{invoiceQuarter} {invoiceYear}, the quarter it was issued in.

bad-debt.title: VAT on unpaid invoices
bad-debt.subtitle: Art. 80.Cuatro of the Spanish VAT Act
bad-debt.what-it-is: The VAT on an invoice is paid over in the 303 of the quarter it was issued in, collected or not. If the client ends up never paying, the law lets you recover the VAT you fronted out of your own pocket: it is called modificación de la base imponible, and it is done by issuing a corrective invoice and notifying the tax office. It is neither automatic nor always available: you have to wait out a term, correct within a six-month window and notify within the following month. Once that window closes, the right is gone for good.

how.title: The three steps, and their deadlines
how.wait-title: 1. Wait for the debt to count as uncollectible
how.wait-description: Six months or one year have to pass from the accrual date with no payment. The short term is an option for small businesses —available if your turnover in the previous calendar year was 6,010,121.04 € or less— and the law lets you choose between the two.
how.rectify-description: Once the waiting term is over, a six-month window opens to issue it and get it to the client. It is a lapse period: the last day is the last day, with no extension and no fixing it afterwards.
how.notify-description: Within one month of the corrective invoice's date you file form 952 through the AEAT site, after uploading the supporting documents through the electronic register.

attention.hint: The window to correct is open, or opens in less than {days} days.

stage-hint.waiting: The waiting term the law requires has not elapsed, so you cannot issue the corrective invoice yet. What you can get on with is claiming payment and keeping the evidence: that step has to be done first.
stage-hint.in-window: You can issue the corrective invoice now. Once the window closes, the VAT on this invoice stops being recoverable.
stage-hint.window-expired: The window closed with no corrective invoice: under this term, the VAT on this invoice can no longer be recovered. It stays listed so the loss is on record, not so it can be chased.
stage-hint.out-of-scope: Art. 80.Cuatro does not reach this invoice, so no deadline is running for it.

bad-debt.term-choice: The law lets you choose between waiting six months or one year, and the app does not know which you chose: that is why it shows both calendars.
bad-debt.term-unconfirmed: That letting the six-month window lapse still leaves you the one-year one is not confirmed by any tax ruling we could verify. Count on the term you chose from the start, and do not treat the second one as a safety net.
bad-debt.pyme-threshold: The six-month term is available if your turnover in the previous calendar year was 6,010,121.04 € or less.
bad-debt.accrual-note: The deadlines here are counted from the invoice date. The law counts them from the accrual date, which for services is the day they are rendered: if you invoiced when the work ended they match, and if not, these dates may run a few days early or late. Check it before cutting it fine on the last day.

checklist.title: What has to be done, and in this order
checklist.description: These are not formalities: the courts treat the requirements as part of the substance of the right, so skipping one costs the whole VAT amount.

claim-payment.title: Claim the payment and keep the evidence
claim-payment.description: A court claim, a notarial demand or any other means that reliably evidences the claim will do: since 2023 a burofax is accepted, because it records what you sent, to whom and when it was delivered. A phone call or a plain email will not do. Keep the receipt, because it has to be submitted. If the debtor is a public body, what you need is its certificate acknowledging the debt.

book-in-registers.title: Have the invoice and the default booked
book-in-registers.description: The transaction has to be invoiced and booked in time and form in the register of issued invoices, and the default reflected in your accounts.

issue-rectificativa.title: Issue the corrective invoice inside the window
issue-rectificativa.description: It corrects the original invoice and its VAT, under its own series. It does not void the invoice or change its status: the transaction happened and still stands.

send-rectificativa.title: Send it to the client and be able to prove it
send-rectificativa.description: Reducing the base is conditional on the corrective invoice being sent to the recipient. No particular means is required, but you do have to be able to prove you sent it.

upload-evidence.title: Upload the documents through the electronic register
upload-evidence.description: A copy of the corrective invoice, showing the date of the invoice it corrects; the evidence of the claim; and, if the debtor is a public body, its certificate. The register returns a code: keep it, because it goes on form 952.

file-modelo-952.title: File form 952 within one month
file-modelo-952.description: One month from the date of the corrective invoice, electronically. On it you declare that the debt is not secured, guaranteed or insured, that it is not between related parties, and that the client is established in Spain.

adjust-303.title: Carry the reduction into the 303
adjust-303.description: The recovered VAT goes into the return for the relevant period. Your client, for their part, has to reduce the VAT they deducted; their failing to do so does not block you.

upward-revision.title: If you do end up getting paid
upward-revision.description: Once corrected, the base is not raised again even if you are eventually paid. But if you withdraw the court claim or agree payment terms with the client, you have one month from that moment to issue another corrective invoice, this time upwards. It is a second clock, and it runs just as fast.

aeat.form: Form 952 — Notification of the modification of the taxable base in insolvency and uncollectible debt cases
aeat.deadline: Filed within one month of the corrective invoice's date.
aeat.deadline-note: The procedure sheet on the AEAT site says «deadline: none». The VAT regulation governs: one month.
aeat.procedure-link: See the procedure on the AEAT site

empty.title: No invoice has the clock running
empty.description: This is where your unpaid invoices whose VAT you can still recover will appear. An empty list does not mean something is missing: if your invoices carry no Spanish VAT, or the client is established outside Spain, the article does not reach them. Every invoice ruled out is listed below with its reason.

no-invoices.title: No invoices are outstanding
no-invoices.description: Every invoice you have issued has been collected. This section only fills up when one goes unpaid.

excluded.title: Invoices ruled out, and why
excluded.description: They are issued and uncollected, but art. 80.Cuatro does not reach them: no deadline is running and there is no right you can lose by doing nothing.

no-output-vat.label: No output VAT
no-output-vat.description: This invoice carries no Spanish VAT, so you fronted nothing and there is nothing to recover. Art. 80.Cuatro only reduces the base of taxed transactions: a corrective invoice here would move 0.00 € in your 303. There is no deadline you can miss and no right you can lose.

recipient-not-established.label: Client not established in Spain
recipient-not-established.description: Your client is not established in Spain, nor in the Canary Islands, Ceuta or Melilla. The law expressly excludes those debts, and on form 952 you have to declare in writing that the invoice is not one with a non-established recipient: filing it for this invoice would be declaring something false. It is not a matter of deadlines — this route is not open to it.

recipient-establishment-unknown.label: Client's country not recorded
recipient-establishment-unknown.description: The invoice does not record the client's country, and whether the article applies depends on that. When in doubt it stays out: better that than pushing you to file a 952 that does not apply. Fill in the country in the client's details and it will be assessed again.

not-issued.label: Not issued or cancelled
not-issued.description: A draft or a cancelled invoice declared nothing and charged no VAT, so there is no VAT fronted to recover.

collected.label: Collected
collected.description: This invoice is recorded as collected, so there is no unpaid debt. If the collection was recorded by mistake or the money was returned, fix the collection first and it will be assessed again.

bad-debt.disclaimer: This is a calendar and a checklist, not a filing: the app does not issue the corrective invoice, does not file form 952 and does not touch the invoice's status. Those steps are yours to take — and if the amount is serious, your accountant's.

aeat.title: How to file in Renta Web
aeat.subtitle: Follow these steps in the Spanish tax portal with the amounts shown above.
aeat.disclaimer: Informational tool. Calculations follow the current crypto regulation (Modelo 100 IRPF). Review with your tax advisor before filing.

casilla-popup.title: Which box do I use? — Virtual currencies, Page 15 (II)
casilla-popup.body:
Crypto sales and swaps (section F2, savings base). Button: "Alta Elemento patrimonial" → one element per coin.

• 1802 — Coin name (one only per element: bitcoin, ethereum…).
• 1803 — Type-of-consideration key: F = sold for euros/fiat · N = swapped for another crypto, NFT, good or service. (F/N goes HERE, NOT in 1804.)
• 1804 — Transmission value (a single amount, net of fees).
• 1806 — Acquisition value (FIFO, net of fees).
• 1807 — Loss (if 1804 − 1806 < 0) · 1809 — Gain (if 1804 − 1806 > 0). Renta Web computes these.

The app's "1804 (F)" and "1804 (N)" buckets are just a grouping by key: in the form, F/N is chosen in box 1803 and the amount goes in box 1804.

Outside Page 15 (II):
• Airdrops / free tokens → box 0304 (section F1, GENERAL base, not a transfer).
• Staking / Earn / lending → box 0033 (section B, income from movable capital, savings base).

casilla-1804-f.title: Selling crypto for euros (key F) — Page 15 (II)
casilla-1804-f.intro: Capital gains and losses from selling crypto for euros or other legal-tender currency (section F2, savings tax base). Each coin is filed as its own "Elemento patrimonial".
steps: In Renta Web open "Page 15 (II)", section "F2. Capital gains and losses from the transfer of assets (savings tax base)", subsection "transfer or exchange of virtual currencies by individuals".
Click "Alta Elemento patrimonial". This creates an "Elemento patrimonial X de Y": one per distinct coin you sold.
In box 1802 enter the coin's name (e.g. bitcoin, ethereum). Each element holds ONE coin only; if you sold several, add a new element for each.
In box 1803 ("type of consideration key") choose F, because you received euros or other legal-tender money.

In box 1804 enter that coin's transmission value and in box 1806 the acquisition value (FIFO), as shown above. Renta Web computes the gain (box 1809) or loss (box 1807) and moves it to the savings tax base.
casilla-1804-f.note: Remember: box 1804 is only the transmission value; what marks it as a fiat sale is key F in box 1803. Losses can be offset against gains of the same group over the next 4 fiscal years.

casilla-1804-n.title: Crypto-to-crypto swaps (key N) — Page 15 (II)
casilla-1804-n.intro: Exchanges of one crypto for another crypto, NFT, good or service (BTC↔ETH, swap to USDT, dust, etc.). Same screen as fiat sales but with key N. Valued at the EUR price of each operation.
steps: On the same "Page 15 (II)" click "Alta Elemento patrimonial" to create one element per coin you swapped.
In box 1802 enter the coin you gave up (one per element) and in box 1803 choose key N (non-fiat: you received another crypto, an NFT, a good or a service).
In box 1804 enter the transmission value (EUR market value of what you received) and in box 1806 the acquisition value (FIFO). The system computes the gain (1809) or loss (1807).

Create one element per distinct coin: box 1802 only accepts a single denomination, so do NOT merge different coins into one row. Within the same coin you may consolidate FIFO lots into a single element; keep the per-operation detail ("Disposals detail" tab) as backup.
casilla-1804-n.note: Key N (box 1803) means non-fiat consideration; box 1804 is still only the transmission value. Keep the per-operation breakdown in case of an audit.

casilla-0304.title: Box 0304 — Airdrops and other capital gains
casilla-0304.intro: Airdrops, Launchpool rewards not derived from staking, and crypto promotions received. NOT a transfer: it goes in the general base.
steps: This amount does NOT go on Page 15 (II). Go to section "F1. Capital gains and losses not derived from the transfer of assets (to be included in the general tax base)".
Find box 0304 ("Other capital gains attributable to the year not derived from a transfer").
Enter the amount in euros: the market value of each airdrop or free token at the exact moment of receipt, summed for the whole year.
Taxed in the GENERAL tax base (progressive 19%-47% scale), not the savings base, and cannot be offset against savings-base losses.
casilla-0304.note: The value you declare here becomes the acquisition value of those tokens: when you later sell or swap them, the gain or loss goes to Page 15 (II), boxes 1804/1806.

casilla-0033.title: Box 0033 — Income from movable capital (staking)
casilla-0033.intro: Staking rewards, Earn flexible/locked, ETH staking and on-chain interest. Declared at market value at the time of receipt.
steps: Go to section B "Income from movable capital" (Page 5), subsection "Income from movable capital to be included in the savings tax base".
Find box 0033 "Income from annuities arising from the investment of capital and other income from movable capital to be included in the savings tax base".
Enter the total amount in euros, summing all rewards for the year at their market value on the day you received them.
Taxed in the savings base (same brackets as dividends, 19%-30%), as income from movable capital.
casilla-0033.note: The acquisition cost of the received tokens equals the declared value, which prevents double taxation if you sell them later.

csv.title: Import exchange CSV

binance.name: Binance
binance.subtitle: Useful to recover older C2C trades (the API only returns the last 6 months) and for reconciliation.
binance.step-1: Sign in to Binance.com and go to Orders → Asset History, then click the export icon (top right) → Export Transaction Records, or go directly {link}.
binance.step-2: Under Time Range, click Customize and select the full period from when you first started using Binance until today.
binance.step-3: Select CSV and click Generate. Wait for the file to be ready, then download it.
binance.step-4: Unzip the archive and upload the CSV here.

kraken.name: Kraken
kraken.subtitle: Export your full Ledgers history so deposits, withdrawals, trades and staking rewards are reconciled.
kraken.step-1: Sign in to Kraken.com and open History → Export, or go directly {link}.
kraken.step-2: Choose the "Ledgers" report and select the full date range from your first activity until today.
kraken.step-3: Click Submit, wait for the export to finish, then download it.
kraken.step-4: Unzip the archive if needed and upload the ledgers CSV here.

coinbase.name: Coinbase
coinbase.subtitle: Export the Coinbase transaction report to import buys, sells, conversions, sends and rewards.
coinbase.step-1: Sign in to Coinbase.com and open Reports → Generate report, or go directly {link}.
coinbase.step-2: Choose the transaction history report for all assets and the full date range.
coinbase.step-3: Generate the CSV and download it once it is ready.
coinbase.step-4: Upload the transaction CSV here (the preamble lines are handled automatically).
